frame: Each crop is a rectangle in fractions of the frame, x and y from its top-left corner, cut at native pixels: the same fractions on every arm and on a photograph (weather rubric §3.2). Each is placed by the preset's geometry, not by what one plate draws, so it holds while the picture changes.

crop.why: The nadir: at pitch −88° the frame's center is straight down, where the cells and their shadows are at their least foreshortened.
The limb away from the sun. Pitch −19.8° is the horizon's dip from 400 km, so the limb crosses the frame at mid-height; this cell holds the cloud tops standing into the band.

terminator.why: The limb over the sun's azimuth, where the terminator meets it and the tops lay their shadows on the air. E2's Shadow is scored here and nowhere else (rubric §2).

crop.why: The disk's center, the sub-observer point: the least foreshortened cloud on the face.
The bases over the horizon. At pitch 4° through a 50° lens the horizon sits 0.575 down the frame; the crop holds it and the row of bases above it.
The sea's horizon. At pitch 5° through a 50° lens it sits 0.594 down the frame; the crop holds the deck over it and the water under it.
The layer's underside over the sun. At pitch 15° through a 55° lens the horizon sits 0.757 down the frame, and the camera faces the sun's azimuth, so the crop is the lit base above the glow.
The antisolar point, at the frame's center: the glory's rings and the deck's cells around it.

anchorFrame: Each real-time anchor still has its own rectangle, in that image's pixels from its top-left corner, at the size of its picture's crop cell (720 × 450): the shared fractions can miss an anchor's subject, and a 4K still's fraction would be scaled down. Each is placed by eye on the cloud the picture's crop is there to show, and is cut at native pixels with no scaling.

crop.why: The near field of small cells and their shadows on the sea, the least foreshortened cloud in an oblique frame, as E1's crop is its nadir.
The deck's tops along the limb, the nearest this still has to E2's cloud tops standing into the band.

terminator.why: The tower and the long shadow it lays across the deck, the shadow on the air that E2's terminator crop scores.

crop.why: Two fair-weather cells right of center with their flat bases against the sky, the bases G1's crop holds.
The row of flat bases receding to the horizon under one large cell, as G1's crop holds its bases over the horizon.
The dark base over the flat horizon, as G2's crop holds the deck over the sea's horizon.
The broken layer lit from below over the sun's disk, as G3's crop holds the layer's underside over the glow.
The layer's red underside just above the sun at lower right, the part of the frame lit from below.
The deck's top at the center of the canyon, the cloud surface G4's crop holds around its antisolar point.
The cloud tops at the frame's center seen from above, as G4's crop holds the deck at its center.
